Ashley (runtime): Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak the p95 for route:chat-high jumped ~60ms on canary. Noticed this at 18:02 during the 2pm load test.
Matt (mlperf): ugh. is this the kernel-affinity change that prefers fused-attn2 on A100?
Ashley (runtime): yeah, fused-attn2 became preferred for short sequences. We expected better perf, but batch formation looks different — more microbatches with mixed seq lengths.
Priya: can you paste the perf log snippet?
Ashley (runtime): sure —
```
[2026-03-17T18:02:11Z] route=chat-high p95=220ms p50=35ms tokens_generated=3.4k
[2026-03-17T18:02:11Z] batcher: microbatches=avg 4 -> 2, kernel=fused-attn2, kv_hit=0.74
[2026-03-17T18:02:11Z] previous-canary: p95=160ms, microbatches=avg 6, kernel=stable-attn, kv_hit=0.87
```
Jamal: KV hit drop looks suspicious — did the kernel change affect prefix hashing or KV cache keying?
Ashley (runtime): looked into that — keying unchanged. But the new microbatch pattern reduces contiguous prefix reuse window, so more cold misses.
Matt (mlperf): that matches theory: fewer requests per batch => lower chance for same session prefixes to be cached in LRU window. Combined with fused kernel having slightly higher per-token overhead, p95 suffers.
Perf-bot: perf/regression detected route=chat-high p95 +60ms vs baseline at 2026-03-17T18:02:00Z. Tagging @release and @eng-runtime.
Priya: can we tweak queue policy to prefer batching by session affinity? i.e., delay a few ms to assemble same-session requests before forming a microbatch.
Ashley (runtime): we tested a short affinity-window of 6ms in staging — reduced p95 by ~20ms but increased p50 by 2ms. tradeoff seems fine for SLOs.
Jamal: show the A/B numbers and kernel breakdown pls.
Ashley (runtime): A/B snapshot —
```
A: kernel=fused-attn2, queue=orig, p95=220ms, kv_hit=0.74
B: kernel=fused-attn2, queue=affinity-6ms, p95=200ms, kv_hit=0.80
C: kernel=stable-attn, queue=orig, p95=160ms, kv_hit=0.87
```
Matt (mlperf): interesting that affinity helps but doesn't close the gap to stable-attn. Could be kernel warmup behavior: fused-attn2 has worse first-token latency when microbatch size=1.
Priya: can we add microbatch-size-aware kernel routing? choose fused-attn2 when microbatch>=4 else stable-attn.
Ashley (runtime): prototype routing exists but was gated off; we can enable per-batch kernel decision. Need to ensure safe fallback when device memory shifts.
Jamal: also check continuous-batching heuristics — maybe the batch splitter is favoring size homogeneity too aggressively, causing early splits. The splitter threshold was lowered in the same deploy.
Ashley (runtime): true — splitter threshold went from 0.6 to 0.45 last night. My hunch: combined change -> smaller, more heterogeneous batches -> KV churn + kernel mischoice.
Matt (mlperf): plan: revert splitter to 0.6 on canary + enable affinity-window 6ms + enable kernel-by-microbatch=on for canary. Run 2h load and capture p95, kv_hit, microbatch dist.
Priya: add counters: per-batch kernel_used, microbatch_sz, kv_hits_before, kv_hits_after so we can correlate.
Ashley (runtime): yep will add those. pushing canary config in 5.
Perf-bot: deploy-started canary-config-2026-03-18T18:10Z by Ashley (runtime).
Ashley (runtime): quick interim results after 30m: p95 dropped to 165ms, kv_hit=0.86, microbatch_avg=5.5. Looks promising.
Jamal: great. any regression elsewhere? route=embeddings etc?
Ashley (runtime): embeddings unaffected; it's mostly chat routes with short-turn sequences.
Matt (mlperf): if this holds, let's make the kernel microbatch rule a runtime policy (configurable per-route) and leave splitter threshold at 0.6 globally.
Priya: also add a safety watch: if p95 rises >25ms for 10m post-change, auto-fallback to previous canary.
Ashley (runtime): adding fallback hook now.
Perf-bot: perf/ok route=chat-high p95 within 8% of baseline after config flip at 2026-03-18T18:40Z.
Ashley (runtime): ok closing loop: follow-ups — 1) add microbatch-aware kernel selector tests to nightly perf suite, 2) add KV reuse heatmap to console for top routes, 3) doc the batcher splitter threshold rationale. Anyone want to own doc item 3?
Matt (mlperf): I'll take doc item 3.
Priya: I'll own KV heatmap sprint ticket.
Jamal: I'll add selector tests to nightly.
Ashley (runtime): thanks all. leaving notes in the incident ticket and adding the data snapshots. :thumbsup:
